_: Hand labels for Map 1 -- Exploratory Expedition. Read off the contact sheet from tools/kinds-sheet.js, which draws each distinct printed picture in colour. `kinds` maps a kind id to what the picture is; `palette` maps a background colour to what the square is made of. Re-running tools/extract-map.js --write regenerates the data and tools/label.js re-applies these; tools/lint-map.js then checks the resulting counts against the Diver's Log, which states outright how many shipwrecks, beacons, stingrays and coral this sheet holds.
paletteNotes: Entries 2 and 3 are the sheet's lighter water textures -- the same open water, painted with a wash. Entry 4 is the darker inner shading of a rock block and entry 5 is a single cell taken over by the shipwreck's hull, which is water underneath.

structure._: Hand-authored constants read off the printed sheet and the Diver's Log. These are panel furniture rather than grid content -- there are a handful per map and reading them off is quicker and surer than teaching the extractor to find each one.

flagValues._: Keyed by the cell holding the FLAG ICON, which is the square you must enclose. The numbered badge hangs one cell below on a pole and is a label, not a target -- the 18-point flag at 3,21 proves it, since its badge sits at row 22, off the bottom of the board and impossible to enclose.

structure.diveMarksNote: Row boundaries a dive must get BELOW, from the triangle markers down the right margin. Reaching all three on every dive is the solo game's gold result; the first is the pass/fail line.

wheel._: The turn track is a 24-tick wheel with six numbered entry points, one per face of the die rolled at setup. Ticks 0-11 (clockwise from the top, the sun side) are day; 12-23 are night. Where you start therefore decides how the 24 turns split, which is the whole reason the setup roll exists.
